description.p: Block Wallet is a self-custody cryptocurrency wallet for the Librem 5 and other GTK4 Linux systems. It is meant to run in Phosh at phone size and as a small window when docked.

One BIP39 recovery phrase covers every chain. Send and receive Bitcoin and Litecoin (native SegWit), Ethereum and ERC-20 tokens, Solana and SPL tokens. Ethereum accounts work unchanged on Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche.

Keys are held in an encrypted store under XDG directories and never leave the device. Point every chain at your own node; the defaults are public servers that can see your addresses. A test-network switch covers Bitcoin testnet, Ethereum Sepolia, Solana devnet and Litecoin testnet.

Version 0.1.0 completed its Librem 5 hardware checklist on PureOS 11 (Crimson). Some areas remain unproven: cross-chain swaps through THORChain have never moved real coins, because that network has been halted throughout testing. Treat swap amounts as you would any first use, and keep your recovery phrase written down.

description.p: Monero joins Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Litecoin as a fifth chain, derived from the same recovery phrase.

ul.li: Send and receive Monero. The wallet scans blocks on the device with the private view key, so the node you use learns nothing about your account from a sync.
A wallet created here scans from its own creation. A restored phrase or an imported spend key scans the last month by default, with a restore height in Settings for anything older.
Import a Monero account by its private spend key, and reveal the spend and view keys to move an account to another Monero wallet.
Stagenet is the Monero test network behind the existing Use test networks switch.
Fixed sync loops being duplicated each time Settings was left, which for Monero would have meant two scanners sharing one cache.

description.p: Built and published without a run on the Librem 5. A stagenet send was built, signed, broadcast and reconciled from both ends on a desktop; nothing has moved on mainnet.
A maintenance release: a swap-fee correctness fix and a payout update. The fee is still 1% everywhere it was already disclosed; only which venues actually charge it changes.

ul.li: LI.FI now charges the same 1% wallet fee KyberSwap already did, since this build is registered with LI.FI as an integrator. Previously LI.FI quoted with no fee at all rather than risk every EVM quote being rejected by an unregistered name.

Fixed a bug that would have broken every Solana swap the moment a swap fee was enabled: Jupiter requires a fee account whenever a fee is requested, and the app was never sending one. The fee itself is still not enabled on Solana.
Updated the swap-fee payout address for Ethereum and its L2s.

description.p: Many more tokens, more swap venues, and a sync that no longer slows down as the token list grows.

ul.li: Around 315 bundled tokens, up from 33: roughly 275 ERC-20s across the seven supported EVM networks and the top 40 Solana tokens. Every contract and mint was verified on-chain before inclusion.
Two more swap venues: KyberSwap alongside LI.FI for same-chain swaps, and Maya Protocol alongside THORChain for cross-chain. Venues are compared side by side and the ones that decline say why.
Balances are read in a single batched call per chain, so syncing costs the same with 300 tokens as with 4 and no longer risks rate-limiting a public node.
The swap screen picks tokens through a searchable list rather than a long dropdown.

Empty assets can be hidden from the Assets screen, and the home screen narrows to what you hold once you hold something. A balance that is still syncing, or that could not be fetched, is never treated as empty.
Polygon's native token is now correctly shown as POL rather than MATIC.

Swaps now carry a 1% wallet fee, taken by the exchange itself rather than as a separate transaction. It is shown as a single Swap fee line on every offer and again on the review screen before anything can be confirmed, and where a venue reports its own fee total that figure already includes it.

description.p: First packaged release: Bitcoin, Ethereum (plus L2s), Solana and Litecoin send/receive/lock from one recovery phrase. Verified against the Librem 5 hardware checklist on PureOS 11 (Crimson).
